items.text: Cobalt moves to a new core banking system Saturday, December 12, 00:00 to Sunday, December 13, 12:00 (Central Time). For 36 hours the app is read-only: balances are visible, but no transfers, no peer-to-peer payments, no new cards. Card payments work offline up to $100 per payment. If something goes wrong, the switch can run some hours longer; nobody can say how many.

Small charges nobody recognizes. Since Monday, some customers have seen small card charges they do not recognize, mostly between $0.50 and $5. Screenshots are on X and Reddit; one post with many shares says "Cobalt got hacked". Known: the charges are real; the security team is investigating with the card processor. Not known: how many customers; what caused it; whether customer data was exposed.
items.personal_event: You see a small card charge you do not recognize on your Cobalt card ($2.40).
items.affected_source: week-4 update: about 9,000 customers affected in total (of 2.1M)

items.text: The card processor confirmed a fault that charged some payments twice on November 16 and 17. Separately, a small number of cards were used for test charges of $0.50 to $2 by fraudsters, a common pattern after card numbers are stolen elsewhere, for example on a fake shopping site. Cobalt's own systems were not breached. About 9,000 customers were affected in total.
The core banking switch ended on Sunday, December 13 at 16:10 Central Time, about four hours late. Card payments kept working offline. Transfers queued on Saturday went through by Sunday night.
items.reading: Known crisis outcome (published 16:00): fixes the overrun level for every run, incl. plan_nosurprises.

items.text: Government shutdown. Overnight, Congress missed its funding deadline, and parts of the federal government shut down. Some federal workers have been sent home; others, such as air traffic controllers and TSA officers, must keep working without pay. Nobody knows how long it will last. Known: Social Security payments and the Postal Service continue. Not known: how long it will last; when federal workers will be paid; which services will slow down. Some of Cobalt's paycheck customers work for the federal government or its contractors. Their next federal paycheck is due on December 30.
items.reading: A12; hits federal-employee paycheck customers (P22 in the panel); Postal Service continues, so postal workers are not hit.
items.personal_event: You work for a federal agency: it is shut down, and your December 30 paycheck may not come on time.

items.text: Government shutdown update. The Senate passed a short-term funding bill; the House plans to vote after Christmas. Federal workers have been told they will get back pay once the government reopens. Their December 30 paycheck may be missed.
items.reading: A12 update: back pay promised, Dec 30 paycheck may still be missed; lower severity.
